newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Mutiny detainees freed in Bangui after amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Mutiny detainees freed in Bangui after amnesty.

text.p: All soldiers and civilians detained during Central African Republic's third army mutiny in under a year were released on Monday under an amnesty, state radio reported.
A total of 19 detainees -- eight soldiers and 11 civilians -- were handed over to African mediators, the radio added.
President Ange-Felix Patasse issued a decree on Saturday proclaiming an amnesty for all involved in the revolts, which began over pay and conditions but turned into a campaign to oust him.
The first mutinies were in April and May. The latest mutiny, which began in November 15, degenerated into ethnic bloodshed. African mediators brokered a peace deal in January.
Patasse formed a government of national unity but his supporters hold the main portfolios. Friction has continued between Patasse and the mutineers.
Witnesses report sporadic gunfire from rebel strongholds this month. Mediators have proposed disarmament of mutineers from March 20-29.
French troops, in the country under a defence pact, restored order after the latest revolt. African peacekeepers have been taking their place.
